Already handled

It knows SAP Business One’s quirks

The things a first SAP Business One integration learns the hard way, written into the connector so yours doesn’t have to.

01

tNO is not true

B1 answers booleans as strings, and (bool) 'tNO' is true in PHP. That is how integrations publish every frozen item. Not this one.

02

Both cookies, every time

On a load-balanced Service Layer the session lives on one node, and ROUTEID is what gets back to it. The connector sends both.

03

20 rows, unless asked

The Service Layer ignores $top without an explicit page-size preference. The connector sets it.

Field mapping

A wrong field is an afternoon, not a release

The connector reads the SKU from ItemCode. If you sell under the barcode, or a user-defined field, one rule points it there.

ReadsWrites
ItemName→title
raw.User_Text→Body
raw.U_WebSKU | trim→skuB1 prefixes user-defined fields U_, and they are all in the raw payload.

Erpy does the rest

Small connector.
Shared engine.

The same order, never twice

A unique database index on every pairing, not a remembered check that could be raced.

Changes only, and none missed

Delta watermarks advance to the start of a run, with overlap, so nothing edited mid-run falls in a gap.

Preview before it writes

A dry run reads a real page and reports what it would create, update or skip.

Nothing lost when refused

A refused document is kept whole on the Problems screen, ready to retry once the cause is fixed.

Checkout never waits

Orders are always pushed from the queue, so a slow or down ERP never delays or fails a sale.

A log that cannot leak

Secrets are stripped from error bodies before a connector, or anyone reading the log, sees them.
